title: AutoEncoder-Compressed Parallel Split Learning for Pre-Trained Model Fine-Tuning
authors: B. Meuwissen, V. Tsouvalas, N. Meratnia
summary: AE-PSL uses a lightweight autoencoder to compress activations and gradients exchanged during parallel split learning. A two-stage alignment procedure adapts the compressor to a pre-trained foundation model and client-specific feature distributions before distributed fine-tuning.

title: Many-Task Federated Fine-Tuning via Unified Task Vectors
authors: V. Tsouvalas, T. Ozcelebi, N. Meratnia
summary: MaTU combines task vectors into a shared representation for federated clients with different or multiple tasks. Lightweight task-specific modulators support transfer between related tasks while separating dissimilar ones, without storing a separate client model at the server.

title: Fine-Tuning Multimodal Transformers on Edge: A Parallel Split Learning Approach
authors: T. Fudala, V. Tsouvalas, N. Meratnia
summary: MPSL fine-tunes multimodal transformers through parallel split learning, using lightweight client tokenizers and a shared modality-agnostic encoder. It reduces client computation while avoiding label sharing, synchronized client execution and separate server models for each client.

title: EFU: Enforcing Federated Unlearning via Functional Encryption
authors: S. Mohammadi, V. Tsouvalas, I. Symeonidis, A. Balador, T. Ozcelebi, F. Flammini, N. Meratnia
summary: EFU uses functional encryption to enforce client-initiated federated unlearning while concealing unlearning requests from the aggregation server. Auxiliary losses aim to hide behavioral and parameter changes while removing the influence of forgotten data.

title: EncCluster: Scalable Functional Encryption in Federated Learning through Weight Clustering and Probabilistic Filters
authors: V. Tsouvalas, S. Mohammadi, A. Balador, T. Ozcelebi, F. Flammini, N. Meratnia
summary: EncCluster combines model weight clustering, decentralized functional encryption and probabilistic filters for secure federated aggregation. The design reduces the amount of data requiring expensive encryption and limits communication overhead on resource-constrained clients.

title: DeltaMask: Minimizing Communication in Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models
authors: V. Tsouvalas, Y. M. Asano, A. Saeed

related.title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models via Probabilistic Masking

summary: DeltaMask adapts vision foundation models in federated learning by learning stochastic masks that select effective subnetworks. It compresses sparse mask updates with probabilistic filters to reduce communication below one bit per model parameter.

title: Labeling Chaos to Learning Harmony: Federated Learning with Noisy Labels
authors: V. Tsouvalas, A. Saeed, T. Ozcelebi, N. Meratnia

related.title: Federated Learning with Noisy Labels: Achieving Generalization in the Face of Label Noise

summary: FedLN addresses noisy labels during federated model initialization, local training and server aggregation. It estimates each client's noise level in a single federated round and uses this estimate to correct labels or reduce the influence of unreliable samples.

title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning through Adaptive Weight Clustering and Server-Side Distillation
authors: V. Tsouvalas, A. Saeed, T. Ozcelebi, N. Meratnia
summary: FedCompress combines adaptive weight clustering with knowledge distillation on the server to reduce federated communication. Its compression strategy targets communication cost and inference efficiency while retaining model generalization.

title: FedCode: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning via Transferring Codebooks
authors: S. Khalilian, V. Tsouvalas, T. Ozcelebi, N. Meratnia
summary: FedCode exchanges codebooks of model-weight cluster centers instead of full weight updates in most federated rounds. Periodic weight transfers recalibrate the client and server models, reducing communication in both directions.

title: On the Effectiveness of Invisible Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
authors: M. Marinus, V. Tsouvalas, N. Meratnia
summary: This study evaluates invisible backdoor attacks in federated learning under different training settings and defenses. It examines how limited local training and model aggregation affect attack success, and investigates attention-based trigger placement.

title: Plug-and-Play Multilingual Few-Shot Spoken Words Recognition
summary: PLiX is a multilingual keyword-spotting approach that recognizes previously unseen spoken words from a few support examples. Models trained on short speech clips from 20 languages are evaluated on new keywords and languages without task-specific retraining.

title: On the Efficacy of Meta-Learning for Domain Generalization in Speech Emotion Recognition
authors: R. K. Gandhi, V. Tsouvalas, N. Meratnia
summary: This study examines domain-shift-aware meta-learning for speech emotion recognition across domains. It identifies limitations of log-mel spectrogram features for domain generalization and explores alternative representations for improving transfer.

title: Federated Self-Training for Semi-Supervised Audio Recognition
authors: V. Tsouvalas, A. Saeed, T. Ozcelebi

related.title: Federated Self-Training for Data-Efficient Audio Recognition

summary: FedSTAR combines federated learning with self-training to use unlabeled audio stored on client devices. It also studies self-supervised pre-training as an initialization that reduces the number of federated training rounds needed for convergence.

title: Privacy-Preserving Speech Emotion Recognition through Semi-Supervised Federated Learning
authors: V. Tsouvalas, T. Ozcelebi, N. Meratnia
summary: This work applies federated self-training to speech emotion recognition using both labeled and unlabeled on-device audio. Experiments on IEMOCAP examine learning with scarce labels and strongly non-IID client data.
